title: Missing Ticket
statement: A raffle sold tickets numbered 1 to n + 1, and the box now holds n tickets in no particular order. Exactly one ticket is missing. Return its number.
constraints: The tickets are distinct numbers from 1 to tickets.length + 1

answerKey.pattern: Sort, then scan for the first position i where the ticket is not i + 1
keyPoints: After sorting, a full set would read 1, 2, 3, … so tickets[i] should equal i + 1
The first i where tickets[i] != i + 1 means i + 1 is missing
If no position breaks the rule, the missing ticket is the last one, n + 1
answerKey.timeComplexity: O(n log n) for the sort
answerKey.spaceComplexity: O(1) extra if sorting in place (the sort itself may use O(log n) to O(n))
edgeCases: Empty box: the missing ticket is 1
The missing ticket is the largest, n + 1
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Checking each number 1..n+1 with a linear search: O(n²)
A faster O(n) answer: the expected sum minus the actual sum, or a hash set

hints: Imagine the tickets lined up in order. What would a complete row look like?
After sorting, position 0 should hold 1, position 1 should hold 2, and so on. Look for the first place that breaks this.
If every position matches, nothing is missing in the middle: the missing ticket is the one after the last, n + 1.
